en.mf.pairs.open.instruction: Tap two that are the same.
en.mf.pairs.open.hint: Find one. Then find another just like it.
en.mf.pairs.instruction: Turn two cards. Find the two that are the same.
en.mf.hidden.incorrect: That one was not there. Think again.
en.mf.earlier.instruction: Think back to the very start. Which of these did you see first?
en.mf.earlier.hint.model: There were two things. One was a cat.
en.mf.order.instruction: Watch the order. Then tap them the same way.
en.mf.groups.instruction: Look. Some of these go together.
en.mf.groups.incorrect: Not quite. Think of the ones that go together.
en.mf.groups.hint.model: Think of one kind. Then think of the other kind.
en.mf.story.instruction: Look who has what. Make a silly picture in your head.
en.mf.story.correct: Yes. That is what it had.
en.mf.story.incorrect: That was not this one’s. Think again.
en.mf.story.hint.model: Have another look. Make a silly picture in your head.
en.mf.places.instruction: Look where each thing is. Walk the path in your head.
en.mf.places.correct: Yes. That is what was there.
en.mf.places.incorrect: That was not at this place. Think again.
en.mf.places.hint.model: Have another look. Walk the path in your head.
en.mf.way.instruction: Look at these four. Tap a picture below to look another way.
en.mf.way.incorrect: Not that one. Think how you looked at them.
en.mf.all.instruction: Now with no help. Which four did you see?
en.mf.all.incorrect: Not quite. Think how you looked at them.
en.mf.five.instruction: Look. There are five this time. Some go together.
en.mf.keep.instruction: These three are for next time. Look well.
en.mf.keep.correct: Yes. Keep them in your head. I will ask you next time.
en.mf.keep.hint.model: Say their names in your head.
en.mf.keep.hint.step: This one is for next time.
en.mf.back.instruction: Think back to last time. Which three did you keep?

skills.title: Find pairs among cards face down
skills.objective: Finds every pair among six or eight cards lying face down, in no more turns than remembering where things are would need.

skills.title: Know again what was just hidden
skills.objective: After looking at two to four things that are then covered, picks out one that was there from pictures of things that were not.

skills.title: Know again what was seen a while ago
skills.objective: At the end of an activity, picks out a thing shown at its very start and not seen since. One question, kept apart from the others: a longer wait is a different thing to manage.

skills.title: Remember an order
skills.objective: Watches three or four things light up one after another and taps them in the same order.

skills.title: Remember by grouping
skills.objective: Looks at four things that fall into two kinds, and after they are put away picks all four out from among others, with nothing to prompt them.

skills.title: Remember by linking two things
skills.objective: Looks at two or three pairs — who had what — and, shown one of them, says what went with it.

skills.title: Remember by places
skills.objective: Looks at things left at two or three places and, shown one place, says what was there.

skills.title: Recall from a hint, looking your own way
skills.objective: Chooses how to look at four things (in groups, as a silly story, or at places) and, when they are put away and a hint is given, says what went with it. Which way was chosen is written down with each answer.

skills.title: Recall four things with no hint
skills.objective: Straight after that, picks all four out from among eight with no hint at all. Counted apart from the question with a hint: what a hint brings back and what comes back by itself are different things.

skills.title: Recall five things
skills.objective: Looks at five things of two kinds, none of them met in the earlier activities, and after they are put away picks all five out from among eight.

skills.title: Take in three things to keep
skills.objective: Looks at three things to keep for next time and picks them out straight away. This shows only that they were taken in; whether they were kept is asked at the next visit.

skills.title: Recall them later the same day
skills.objective: At the start of a later visit on the same day, ten minutes or more after the three things were shown, picks them out with nothing shown again.

skills.title: Recall them on another day
skills.objective: At the start of a visit on a later day, picks out the three things kept, with nothing shown again. Kept apart from the same day: a night between is a different wait.

lessons.title: Find the pairs
lessons.summary: Cards lie in rows, two of each picture. First they are face up, to learn how the game goes; then face down, two turned at a time. A pair stays turned; two that differ are looked at and turn back.

lessons.title: Which one was there?
lessons.summary: Two, three or four things are shown, and then a big leaf covers them. Your child says which of some pictures was under the leaf. The others were never there, though some are the same kind of thing. At the very end there is one question about the first things shown, which have not been seen since.

lessons.title: The same order
lessons.summary: Animals light up one after another, each with its name, and your child taps them in the same order: two at first, then three, then four. Seeing the order again is help, and is asked for as help.

lessons.title: Things that go together
lessons.summary: Four things are shown, two of one kind and two of another: two animals and two things to wear, say. Then they are put away and your child picks them out from among others. Thinking of them as two pairs is easier than four separate things, and that is the trick being practised.

lessons.title: Who had what?
lessons.summary: Animals are shown, each with a thing: the cat has the hat, the fox has the drum. Then they are hidden and your child is shown one animal and asked what it had. Making a silly picture in your head of the two together is the trick: say it aloud with your child, the sillier the better.

lessons.title: What was where?
lessons.summary: Things are left at places along a path: on the log, in the nest, by the hut. Then they are hidden and your child is shown one place and asked what was there. Walking the path in your head, place by place, is the trick. It works at home too: what is by the door, on the stairs, on the bed?

lessons.title: Remember it your way
lessons.summary: Four things are shown, and your child chooses how to look at them: in two groups, as a silly story of who has what, or at places along a path. Then one question with a hint, and one with none: which four were they? The two are counted apart.

lessons.title: Keep it for next time
lessons.summary: First, five things to look at and pick out again: one more than before, and all new. Then three things to keep. Your child picks them out once now, and is asked for them again at the start of the next visit, ten minutes later or another day, with nothing shown.
